1963 Ford Galaxie 500 Convertible
A complete visual journey from a tired blue survivor to a refined white-and-turquoise American classic. This Fitzgerald Classics restoration follows the Galaxie through body preparation, paint, interior reconstruction, detail work and final assembly—preserving the character of Ford’s full-size 1960s convertible while giving every surface the attention it deserved.
The Starting Point — For Sale
The Galaxie as found: dark blue, white convertible top, and still wearing its For Sale signs.
Original Profile
A full side view showing the Galaxie's original dark blue presentation before restoration.
Original Front End
A closer look at the original paint, grille, trim, and front-end condition before work began.
Original Galaxie 500 Trim
A detail view of the original Galaxie 500 fender emblem and dark blue finish.
Original Interior
The turquoise interior before restoration, showing the condition of the dash, steering wheel, seating, and door panel.
Interior Wear Before Restoration
A close view of the front bench seat and interior trim before refurbishment.
Original Engine Bay
The engine compartment as acquired, before the restoration and mechanical refresh.
Underhood Condition
A wider record of the engine bay and underside of the hood before the mechanical and cosmetic work progressed.
Mechanical Work Begins
Early hands-on work in the engine bay marks the beginning of the restoration process.
Engine Tear-Down and Service
Mechanical work underway as the Galaxie moves from survivor condition into restoration.
Engine Out — Bay Ready
With the engine removed, the Galaxie's engine bay is exposed and ready for the next phase of restoration.
289 Rebuild — Fresh Block
The Ford small-block begins its rebuild with the cleaned and machined block prepared for assembly.
New Pistons Installed
Fresh pistons and machined cylinder surfaces mark a major step in rebuilding the Galaxie's V8.
Cylinder Head Rebuilt
A rebuilt cylinder head with renewed valvetrain components prepared for installation.
Cylinder Head — Finished Surface
The machined combustion chambers and valves show the detail behind the engine rebuild.
289 V8 Reassembled
The rebuilt 289 takes shape with fresh components and a clean, purposeful presentation.
289 Powered by Ford
The completed engine wears its finished valve covers and ignition components before returning to the car.
Engine Ready for Installation
The rebuilt Ford V8 is complete and ready to be reunited with the Galaxie.
Final Engine Detail
A final view of the completed 289 before installation, highlighting the clean mechanical restoration.
Brightwork Restored
Refinished grille and trim pieces prepared for reassembly as the cosmetic restoration moves forward.
Rear Panel — Final Bodywork
The rear body panel is stripped and refined as the Galaxie moves into its final paint-preparation stage.
Color Goes On
Fresh Wimbledon White begins transforming the car in the paint booth, marking the visual turning point of the restoration.
Fresh from the Booth
The body emerges in fresh white paint, with trim still removed and the clean lines of the Galaxie fully exposed.
Trunk Lid — Finished Inside and Out
The underside of the trunk lid receives the same careful finish as the exterior, completing another often-overlooked detail.
Rear Body in Fresh Paint
With the rear lamps and brightwork removed, the newly painted body shows the restoration at its cleanest stage before reassembly.
Paint Finish — Final Inspection
The fresh white finish is inspected under shop lighting before the Galaxie begins its final reassembly.
Tail Lamp and Quarter Trim Return
Restored tail-lamp hardware and quarter-panel trim begin returning the Galaxie's signature details to the freshly painted body.
Chrome Reassembly
The long side moldings and polished quarter trim are carefully refitted, bringing definition back to the Galaxie's sweeping profile.
Galaxie 500 Details Return
The front-fender brightwork and Galaxie 500 emblem return to the car as the exterior nears completion.
Rebuilt 289 Back Home
The rebuilt 289 is back in the freshly restored engine bay as the mechanical and cosmetic restoration finally come together.
Reassembly Begins
With paint and major mechanical work behind it, the Galaxie begins the careful process of coming back together.
Fresh Paint, Bare Details
The newly finished body is ready for the chrome, trim, lighting and hardware that define a 1963 Galaxie.
Brightwork Returns
Restored exterior trim begins returning to the car, bringing contrast and character back to the fresh finish.
Chrome and Trim Fitment
Piece by piece, the polished moldings and trim are aligned and refitted to the body.
Rear Details Rebuilt
The rear of the Galaxie starts regaining its unmistakable 1963 styling as the finishing pieces go back on.
Front End Comes Together
Lighting, trim and front-end details are restored and reinstalled as the exterior nears completion.
Galaxie 500 Identity
The signature emblems and brightwork return, restoring the car's original visual identity.
Mechanical Reassembly
The restored mechanical systems are brought back together with the same attention given to the body and trim.
Engine Bay Finalization
The engine compartment moves from restoration work to final detailing and functional assembly.
Systems Back Online
Cooling, ignition, fuel and accessory systems are completed as the Galaxie prepares to return to the road.
Interior Restoration Begins
Attention turns inside, where the cabin receives the same careful restoration as the exterior.
Dash and Controls
The dashboard, instruments and controls are refreshed to preserve the Galaxie's period-correct character.
Cabin Details Return
Interior trim and hardware are reinstalled as the restored cabin begins taking shape.
Seating Restored
The seating is refreshed to complement the car's restored turquoise interior and classic full-size Ford style.
Door Panels and Trim
Door panels and interior brightwork are restored and fitted, finishing another major part of the cabin.
Turquoise Cabin Returns
The restored interior color and trim bring the Galaxie's early-1960s personality back to life.
Convertible Details
Top, weather sealing and convertible-specific trim are brought together as the restoration enters its final stretch.
Final Exterior Assembly
The remaining exterior pieces are installed and aligned, completing the Galaxie's long, sweeping body lines.
Wheels and Stance
With the finishing details in place, the restored Galaxie begins to look complete from every angle.
The Transformation Takes Shape
Fresh paint, brightwork and restored mechanicals now read as one cohesive finished car.
Final Fit and Finish
Panel alignment, trim placement and presentation details are checked before the car's final reveal.
Detailing the Finished Car
The restored surfaces receive their final attention, sharpening the contrast between white paint, chrome and turquoise accents.
Engine Bay Complete
The rebuilt 289 and restored engine compartment are complete, clean and ready for the road.
Interior Complete
The finished cabin brings back the color, comfort and unmistakable style of Ford's 1963 full-size convertible.
Front Three-Quarter Reveal
The completed Galaxie shows off its restored proportions, brightwork and crisp white finish.
Rear Three-Quarter Reveal
From the rear, the restored tail treatment and long quarter panels show why the Galaxie remains such an iconic American design.
Top Down Classic
With the convertible opened up, the restored Galaxie returns to the form it was built to be enjoyed in.
Full Side Profile
The finished side view highlights the Galaxie's length, clean character line and restored chrome.
Finished Front Detail
Chrome, lighting and paint come together in the completed front end.
Finished Rear Detail
The restored rear treatment finishes the car with the period styling that made the Galaxie distinctive.
Preserving the Details
Small emblems, trim pieces and finishing touches complete the restoration without erasing the car's original character.
Ready for the Road
After mechanical, body, paint, trim and interior work, the Galaxie is once again ready to be driven and enjoyed.
1963 Ford Galaxie 500 — Restored
The finished result: a classic American convertible brought back with respect for its original style and a focus on workmanship throughout.
